middle.heading: About Me
middle.intro: I’m a software engineer with 5+ years of experience building reactive, user-friendly web components. I’m also an amateur frog enthusiast with 28+ years experience. My recent work has largely been in TypeScript, SolidJS, and Angular, but I’m more interested in providing a rich user experience than in using any particular framework or language. Lately I’ve been getting reacquainted with React, and I’m enjoying it so far. When it comes to amphibians, most of my hands-on experience has been in northwestern Pennsylvania, but I’m interested in critters of all kinds and locales.
middle.contact: Here’s {resume}, or you can {email} directly. I’m also on {linkedIn}, and you can check out the code for this site on my {gitHub}.

about.heading: About
about.lead: This site is an exploration in building software with Claude. For this project I wanted to experiment with different methods of Claude‑assisted development, working faster and trying new approaches. Claude helped plan features, orchestrate agents, maintain design paradigms and review the code, while I set the standards, made the calls and reviewed the changes before committing. I used Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 for planning, building and orchestrating, and Sonnet 5.5 for the parallel agents. I also built on the habits from my first Claude project (ToDoApp, on {gitHub}), which served as a style guide. Here’s the workflow I ended up with, and the lessons that shaped it.

loop.heading: The loop
loop.caption: Every sizeable feature on this site went through these steps. Deciding and committing stay with me.
loop.loopback: {label} wherever the code ended up differing from the plan gets written down, and that feeds the next plan.

plan.title: Plan
plan.body: A Markdown plan for each sizeable feature: the goal, the decisions, the steps and a test strategy, with the how and the why of each step. Plans live outside the repo, so the codebase stays clean.

reviewPlan.title: Review the plan
reviewPlan.body: A new session with no stake in the plan checks it against the actual code and current library APIs: is it sound, are there security gaps, will it run, are the package versions current?

decide.title: Decide
decide.body: I settle every open decision, and push back wherever the plan isn’t what I want.

build.title: Build
build.body: Claude implements the plan step by step, running the tests as it goes.

prove.title: Prove
prove.body: Unit tests, integration tests against a real database, real-browser tests at nine screen sizes, an accessibility scan and a smoke test of the production image. Each new test is broken on purpose once, to show it can fail.

reviewChange.title: Review the change
reviewChange.body: A deliberately hostile review that looks for every way the change is wrong, fragile, insecure or hard to test.

commit.title: Commit
commit.body: Claude never commits. I read the diff and commit it myself.

passes.heading: Scaling up: orchestrated passes
passes.caption: The loop at a larger scale: the same plan, review and verify steps, run in parallel.
passes.lensesLabel: Each reviewer reads through five lenses:

split.title: Split
split.body: For a repo-wide quality pass, the codebase is cut into slices.

review.title: Review in parallel
review.body: One reviewer per slice, side by side, each reading whole files, not just a diff.

verify.title: Verify
verify.body: Every finding is checked against the code itself before it reaches a plan.

fix.title: Fix in parallel
fix.body: Each plan runs as its own agent, in its own git worktree.

merge.title: Merge
merge.body: Each merge is reviewed before it lands in my working tree, uncommitted, for me to review.

guardrails.heading: Guardrails: rules Claude can’t forget
guardrails.caption: Each layer catches what slipped past the one above it, and most of them exist because of a mistake. A change that breaks the house rules fails loudly, no matter who or what wrote it.

rulebook.name: The rulebook (CLAUDE.md)
rulebook.catches: Loaded into every session: the conventions, the deliberate exceptions, and the bar for calling work done

conventions.name: Convention tests
conventions.catches: Colours only from the palette, sizes in rem, every word from the dictionary

contrast.name: Computed contrast
contrast.catches: Every colour pairing checked against WCAG AA, in both themes

browser.name: Real browser and axe
browser.catches: Layout at nine screen sizes; accessibility rules on every page

integration.name: Integration and smoke tests
integration.catches: A real database; the production image’s headers, caching and limits

ci.name: CI and Dependabot
ci.catches: Every push; a vulnerable package fails the build

sentences.title: Fix bugs while they’re still sentences
sentences.happened: An early plan rested on a wrong assumption about how one of the tools worked. A review caught it before any code existed.
sentences.now: Nothing bigger than a tweak starts without a reviewed plan.

freshEyes.title: Get a fresh pair of eyes
freshEyes.happened: A new session reviewing a plan found a long list of problems that the session that wrote it had missed.
freshEyes.now: The session that wrote something never reviews it.

makeItATest.title: If it matters, make it a test
makeItATest.happened: In my first project, the styling conventions lived in my head and in prose.
makeItATest.now: Here they are tests, so a stray colour or a hard-coded word fails the build.

canFail.title: A test that can’t fail isn’t a test
canFail.happened: Some early assertions turned out to check nothing at all.
canFail.now: Every plan has a breakage step: break the code, watch the test fail, put it back.

compute.title: Compute, don’t estimate
compute.happened: Estimated colour contrast ratios didn’t hold up when they were actually measured.
compute.now: A test computes every pairing straight from the palette.

realBrowser.title: A simulated browser isn’t a browser
realBrowser.happened: A layout bug that the simulated-browser tests passed showed up only in a real browser.
realBrowser.now: Layout and focus changes get real-browser tests.

setupFirst.title: Check the setup before the code
setupFirst.happened: A failed deploy sent Claude hunting through the code when the real problem was a skipped setup step.
setupFirst.now: Deploy problems start with the hosting checklist.

knowYourMachine.title: Know your machine
knowYourMachine.happened: A few quirks of my development setup caused confusing failures that had nothing to do with the code.
knowYourMachine.now: Each workaround is written into the project’s instructions for Claude, so no session trips on the same one twice.

next.heading: What’s next
next.body: An admin page for managing the site, more frogs, a way for visitors to submit their own frogs, and more.

about.body: All images and drawings on the site are my own, so no need for licensing. I’m just a casual frog enjoyer, and I didn’t want to wing it, so all frog facts on this site (excluding those about cats) came from paherps.com.
